title: Efficient Diffusion Policies for Offline Reinforcement Learning

methods.one_paragraph_description: Efficient Diffusion Policy (EDP): DDPM noise-prediction policy trained with action approximation (reconstruct a clean action from a noised dataset action in one network pass instead of running the K-step chain), sampled with DPM-Solver (15 model calls); at evaluation, energy-based action selection over N=10 sampled actions weighted by exp(Q). Trained with the Diffusion-QL objective (TD loss + weighted policy loss) with K=1000; reported with OMS metric.
methods.conventional_lineage_hint: offline RL, diffusion policy class ('Diffusion policy has emerged as an expressive policy class for offline reinforcement learning'); plug-in for direct (TD3) and likelihood-based (CRR, IQL) policy optimization

backbone.quote: We keep the backbone network architecture the same for all tasks and algorithms, which is a 3-layer MLP (hidden size 256) with Mish [23] activation function following Diffusion-QL [37].

optimizer.quote: We use the Adam [13] to optimize both diffusion policy and the Q networks.

epochs.quote: The models are trained for 2000 epochs on Gym-locomotion and 1000 epochs on the other three domains.

iterations_per_epoch.quote: Each epoch consists of 1000 iterations of policy updates with batch size 256.

learning_rate.location: Table 3 (columns: Learning rate, Gradient norm clipping, Loss weight, Epochs, Batch size)

sampler.quote: For DPM-Solver [20], we use the third-order version and set the model call steps to 15.

sampler_steps.quote: The performance gradually plateaus after 15 model calls. Therefore, we use 15 in our main experiments.

diffusion_steps_K.quote: This enables EDP to use a larger K (1000 in our experiments) to train diffusion policy on the more fine-grained scale.

eas_num_actions_N.quote: In our main experiments, we set the number of actions to 10 by trading off the performance and computation efficiency.

action_selection.value: energy-based action selection: sample N actions, pick one with weights ∝ exp(Q)
action_selection.quote: EAS first samples N actions from πθ by using any samplers (i.e., DPM-Solver), then sample one of them with weights proportional to eQ(s,a) .

seeds.quote: Throughout this paper, the results are reported by averaging 5 random seeds.
